chapter: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
title: Martin Block won't plug Lu's records; Hot Dog, That Lady's Bad
summary: Danny asked disc jockey Martin Block to play Lu's records, and he and Lu recall the lyrics of Hot Dog, That Lady's Bad.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: That's who came in (?) night. Martin Block. He had the biggest show on radio. When I approached him in the (?) and asked him, "Have you heard my wife?" He said, "Yes, I have." I said, "Will you give our records a plug?" He said, "Yes, I'll plug them sometimes," just like that. I expected him to say something, "Oh yeah..." But he was so cool, the way he was... But he was plugging, like, Monica Lewis and Monica Boyer, and you know, a gang of singers out there... But he was looking right at her, and he (?)ain't plugged(?) nothin'... But I guess it was suggested through them records, you know, "Feel My Leg," "Hot Dog, That Lady's
That's another one. I forgot about that.
"Hot Dog, That Lady's Bad." How did the lyrics go on that? I forgot that lyric.

"Got a man,/He's long and tall,/Won't let me have no pleasure at all./He's jealous of my neighbors and all of my friends,/And last night I sneaked out with a long man./That man ain't married(?)./Hot dog, that lady's bad."
"Do I hug and kiss him/And say I wouldn't do it no mo'." One more time. "When I want..."
"Tuesday night, I did so-and-so..." We had a whole thing.
